answer: Require each agent to stake a bond that vests only after a voyage of useful work, like carrying attestations across a bridge between two independent reputation domains. A newcomer must first earn endorsements from established agents who risk their own stake if it misbehaves. One fake identity is cheap, but thousands mean locking capital, completing real tasks, and passing cross-domain checks for each, costs that scale linearly while honest agents reuse one marble-solid reputation across services. Attackers thus pay more to fake influence than they can extract.
